method_card.title: Family and Describing People
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family vocabulary, possessive adjectives and how to describe appearance and personality in French.

FrenchEnglish
le pèrefather
la mèremother
le frèrebrother
la sœursister
le grand-pèregrandfather
la grand-mèregrandmother
l'oncleuncle
la tanteaunt
le cousin / la cousinecousin
le filsson
la filledaughter
le beau-pèrestepfather
la belle-mèrestepmother
le demi-frère / la demi-sœurhalf-brother / half-sister
les parentsparents

Possessive adjectives agree with the noun they describe, not the owner: mon (m. sg.), ma (f. sg.), mes (pl.) = my; son (m. sg.), sa (f. sg.), ses (pl.) = his/her. Important exception: before a feminine noun starting with a vowel or silent h, use mon/ton/son instead of ma/ta/sa — e.g. mon amie (not ma amie).

Describing people: Use avoir for hair and eyes — Il a les cheveux blonds et les yeux bleus. (He has blond hair and blue eyes.) Use être for build and personality — Elle est grande et sympa. (She is tall and nice.) Adjectives must agree in gender and number with the noun they describe.

Model paragraph: Mon père s'appelle Jules. Il a les cheveux courts et bruns et les yeux noisette. Il est grand et très gentil. Ma mère s'appelle Isabelle. Elle est petite et amusante. (My father is called Jules. He has short brown hair and hazel eyes. He is tall and very kind. My mother is called Isabelle. She is short and fun.)

method_card.title: Friendships and Personal Qualities
method_card.content:
This lesson covers friendship vocabulary, the qualities you look for in a friend, and how to use opinion verbs and the near future tense to talk about spending time together.

FrenchEnglish
un(e) ami(e)a friend
le/la meilleur(e) ami(e)best friend
s'entendre bien avecto get on well with
se disputer avecto argue with
passer du temps avecto spend time with
la confiancetrust
le soutiensupport
fidèleloyal
honnêtehonest
drôlefunny
patient(e)patient
égoïsteselfish
je pense que / je trouve queI think that
à mon avisin my opinion

Near future tense: Use the present tense of aller + infinitive to say what you are going to do. Je vais sortir avec mes amis = I am going to go out with my friends. Nous allons jouer au foot = We are going to play football. This is the most natural way to add a future time frame in spoken and written French.

Opinion verbs: je pense que, je trouve que, à mon avis are followed by a full clause. Example: Je pense que la confiance est très importante dans l'amitié. (I think that trust is very important in friendship.)

Model paragraph: Mon meilleur ami s'appelle Karim. Je m'entends très bien avec lui car il est fidèle et honnête. Il m'écoute toujours quand j'ai un problème. Ce week-end, nous allons jouer au foot ensemble. (My best friend is called Karim. I get on very well with him because he is loyal and honest. He always listens to me when I have a problem. This weekend we are going to play football together.)

method_card.title: Relationships and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers relationships and family life vocabulary, pros and cons of marriage, and how to talk about future plans using the conditional tense.

FrenchEnglish
le couplecouple
le/la partenairepartner
le mariagemarriage / wedding
se marierto get married
le PACScivil partnership
se séparerto separate
célibatairesingle
l'amourlove
sortir avecto go out with
tomber amoureux/amoureuseto fall in love
je voudraisI would like
j'aimeraisI would like
ce seraitit would be
à l'avenirin the future

The conditional tense expresses what you would like to do. For most verbs: take the infinitive and add the imperfect endings (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient). Common irregular stems: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, vouloir → voudr-. The most useful forms at GCSE are: je voudrais (I would like), j'aimerais (I would like), ce serait (it would be).

Usage: After je voudrais / j'aimerais, use an infinitive: Je voudrais me marier un jour. (I would like to get married one day.) After ce serait + adjective + de, also use an infinitive: Ce serait idéal d'habiter à la campagne. (It would be ideal to live in the countryside.)

Model paragraph: À l'avenir, je voudrais me marier et avoir deux enfants. Cependant, je pense qu'on peut être heureux sans se marier. Un PACS est plus simple et moins cher. (In the future, I would like to get married and have two children. However, I think you can be happy without getting married. A civil partnership is simpler and cheaper.)

method_card.title: Equality and Inclusion
method_card.content:
This lesson covers equality and inclusion vocabulary at Higher tier. You will discuss fairness, discrimination and the importance of inclusion using opinion verbs, subordinate clauses and abstract language.

FrenchEnglish
l'égalité (f)equality
l'inégalité (f)inequality
la discriminationdiscrimination
le racismeracism
le sexismesexism
l'homophobie (f)homophobia
juste / injustefair / unfair
défendreto defend / to stand up for
s'engager (pour)to commit (to) / to get involved
l'engagement (m)commitment / engagement
la diversitédiversity
inclusif / inclusiveinclusive
bienveillant(e)kind / compassionate
respectueux / respectueuserespectful
il faut queit is necessary that (+ subjunctive)

Opinion verbs — express abstract views with: je pense que, je trouve que, je crois que, il me semble que, à mon avis. Example: Je pense que la discrimination est injuste et il faut la combattre. (I think discrimination is unfair and we must fight it.)

Connectives for complex sentences: parce que (because), bien que (although — + subjunctive), pourtant (however), cependant (however), malgré (despite). Example: Bien que des progrès aient été faits, l'inégalité existe encore. (Although progress has been made, inequality still exists.)

Higher grammar focus — il faut que + subjunctive: Il faut que chacun soit respectueux. (It is necessary for everyone to be respectful.) The subjunctive of être = soit; of avoir = ait; of faire = fasse.

Model paragraph: À mon avis, la discrimination est complètement injuste. Il faut que tout le monde s'engage pour l'égalité et la diversité. Je crois qu'une société inclusive est plus forte et plus bienveillante. (In my opinion, discrimination is completely unfair. Everyone must get involved in equality and diversity. I believe an inclusive society is stronger and more compassionate.)

method_card.title: Identity and Self-Description
method_card.content:
This lesson covers how to introduce yourself and describe your identity in French — your nationality, the languages you speak, your values and what makes you who you are.

FrenchEnglish
je m'appellemy name is / I am called
j'ai [number] ansI am [number] years old
je suis [nationality]I am [nationality]
anglais(e)English
français(e)French
espagnol(e)Spanish
allemand(e)German
gallois(e)Welsh
écossais(e)Scottish
irlandais(e)Irish
je parle [language]I speak [language]
l'anglais / le français / l'espagnolEnglish / French / Spanish
mes valeursmy values
important(e) pour moiimportant to me

Nationality adjectives agree in gender and number with the person they describe. Masculine: anglais, français, espagnol, allemand, gallois, écossais, irlandais. Feminine: add -e (or change -ais → -aise, -ois → -oise): anglaise, française, espagnole, allemande, galloise, écossaise, irlandaise. Important: nationality adjectives are NOT capitalised in French (unlike in English).

être + adjective: Use être to describe identity and character: Je suis curieux et ouvert d'esprit. (I am curious and open-minded.) Adjectives must agree: masculine curieux, feminine curieuse.

Languages: Say je parle [language] or je parle couramment [language] (I speak [language] fluently). The language names are always lower case: l'anglais, le français, l'espagnol.

Model paragraph: Je m'appelle Sofia. J'ai seize ans et je suis anglaise. Je parle anglais et français. Pour moi, les valeurs les plus importantes sont l'honnêteté et la loyauté. Je suis curieuse et j'adore apprendre de nouvelles choses. (My name is Sofia. I am sixteen and I am English. I speak English and French. For me, the most important values are honesty and loyalty. I am curious and I love learning new things.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — introductions and identity appear in every exam series

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive — être after il est important que (Higher)

wrong.est: est is the indicative. After il est important que, you need the present subjunctive: soit.
wrong.sera: sera is the simple future. After que + subjunctive trigger, use soit.

gaps.correct_explain: soit is the present subjunctive of être. After il est important que, French requires the subjunctive.

wrong.appelle: appelle without the reflexive pronoun is incorrect. S'appeler is reflexive: je m'appelle.

gaps.correct_explain: m'appelle is correct — je m'appelle = my name is / I am called.

gaps.rule: Verb avoir — j'ai (I have/I am for age)

wrong.suis: suis is from être. For age in French, use avoir: j'ai quinze ans, not je suis quinze ans.

gaps.correct_explain: ai is the je form of avoir. French uses avoir (to have) to express age: j'ai quinze ans = I am fifteen.

wrong.anglais: anglais is masculine. The subject is je = Inès (feminine), so you need anglaise.

gaps.correct_explain: anglaise is the feminine form of anglais. Any feminine nationality is acceptable here.

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Je suis anglais et je parle anglais et un peu de français.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Nationality adjectives agree with the person being described. Masculine form is the base: anglais, français, espagnol, gallois.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: To form the feminine, usually add -e. But watch patterns: -ais → -aise (anglais → anglaise), -ois → -oise (gallois → galloise), -ol → -ole (espagnol → espagnole).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Important: nationality adjectives in French are NOT capitalised. Write je suis anglais, not je suis Anglais.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Add -e (or follow the pattern) to form the feminine. Never capitalise nationality adjectives in French.
